explanation.text:
Compare Sa1 21:1-10; Sa1 22:1-10, for the history of the title. Psa 52:1 gives the theme; the boast of the wicked over the righteous is vain, for God constantly cares for His people. This is expanded by describing the malice and deceit, and then the ruin, of the wicked, and the happy state of the pious. (Psa 52:1-9)

mighty man--literally, "hero." Doeg may be thus addressed, ironically, in respect of his might in slander.

bsb.title: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of David. After Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and told him, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.”
bsb.text: Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man? The loving devotion of God endures all day long.

explanation.text:
tongue--for self.

mischiefs--evil to others (Psa 5:9; Psa 38:12).

working deceitfully-- (Psa 10:7), as a keen, smoothly moving razor, cutting quietly, but deeply.

bsb.text: Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, O worker of deceit.

explanation.text:
Thou lovest evil more than good,.... Indeed not good at all; such comparatives being strong negatives; see Psalm 118:8; a wicked man loves evil, and nothing else; his carnal mind being enmity to all that is good

and lying rather than to speak righteousness; as appears by his affirming that Ahimelech inquired of the Lord for David, when he did not, 1 Samuel 22:10; and by suffering some things to pass for truths which were falsehoods, when it lay in his power to have disproved them: and such a lover of lies is antichrist; see 1 Timothy 4:2.

Selah; on this word; see Gill on Psalm 3:2. The Targum renders the word "Selah" here "for ever", as in Psalm 52:5.

bsb.text: You love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking truth. Selah

explanation.text: all-devouring--literally, "swallowing," which utterly destroy (compare Psa 21:9; Psa 35:25).

bsb.text: You love every word that devours, O deceitful tongue.

explanation.text: likewise--or, "so," "also," as you have done to others God will do to you (Psa 18:27). The following terms describe the most entire ruin.

bsb.text: Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin; He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah

explanation.text:
shall . . . fear--regard with religious awe.

laugh at him--for his folly;

bsb.text: The righteous will see and fear; they will mock the evildoer, saying,

explanation.text:
for trusting in riches and being strong in "wickedness."

wickedness--literally, "mischief" (Psa 52:2), instead of trusting in God.

the man--literally, "the mighty man," or "hero" (Psa 52:1).

bsb.text: “Look at the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth and strengthened himself by destruction.”

explanation.text:
The figure used is common (Psa 1:3; Jer 11:16).

green--fresh.

house, etc.--in communion with God (compare Psa 27:4-5).

for ever and ever--qualifies "mercy."

bsb.text: But I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God; I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever.

explanation.text:
hast done--that is, what the context supplies, "preserved me" (compare Psa 22:31).

wait . . . name--hope in Thy perfections, manifested for my good (Psa 5:11; Psa 20:1).

for it is good--that is, Thy name, and the whole method or result of its manifestation (Psa 54:6; Psa 69:16).

Next: Psalms Chapter 53

bsb.text: I will praise You forever, because You have done it. I will wait on Your name—for it is good—in the presence of Your saints.
